headline: Low interaction risk overall: no shared write or MCP surfaces, but A’s broad egress could still leak content if B feeds it documents.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible prompt-injection bridge is documented. Agent A has no listed input surfaces, and agent B has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, MCP, or filesystem write path to pass attacker-controlled text into A by default. The pair lacks a shared communication channel in the profiles.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies B output into A prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF either agent is connected to a shared clipboard or message queue, reassess.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected from shared clipboard channels.
Do not pipe B output directly into A prompts.
Review any orchestrator for hidden prompt concatenation.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any bridged text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B is local-only with no filesystem read or network egress, while A has broad network egress. The profiles do not show a shared workspace or sensitive data class, so leakage is not default. If B processes documents and forwards them to A, A could exfiltrate that content over the network.
conditions: IF B is given sensitive documents and an orchestrator forwards them to A, leakage risk increases.
IF A is connected to any external API endpoint, content can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Do not route sensitive files from B into A.
Disable A network access when handling confidential material.
Use a redaction step before any handoff.
Log all cross-agent transfers for review.
requires-engineering: enforce an allowlist for outbound destinations.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write or mutable-resource capabilities are documented. A has no filesystem or git write surface in the profile, and B explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. Without shared writable state, capability conflict is not plausible.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, reassess conflict risk.
IF either agent gains git or database write scopes, conflict risk changes.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in shared environments.
Separate any writable workspaces by agent.
Avoid granting git write permissions to either agent.
requires-engineering: add locking for any future shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a document-processing agent, so it may consume A’s outputs as inputs, but the profiles do not show B taking downstream actions or A producing authoritative facts. The main risk is misinterpretation of A’s content if an orchestrator chains them without verification.
conditions: IF B is configured to treat A output as authoritative input, cascading error risk increases.
IF B is connected to an action-taking downstream system, impact becomes larger.
mitigations: Insert a verification step between A and B.
Require human review of A outputs before B consumes them.
Limit A outputs to summaries with source links.
Track provenance on all A-to-B handoffs.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for A outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced. Neither profile lists regulated data classes, residency constraints, retention policies, or certifications, and both are docs-only/open-source entries. With no documented sensitive-data flow, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, reassess compliance.
IF residency or retention requirements are introduced, compare them explicitly.
mitigations: Document the data classes before deployment.
Avoid sending regulated data through either agent.
Add a retention policy review before rollout.
requires-engineering: map data flows to residency controls.
